messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated TLS handshake failures (client-timeout/connection reset) observed for api.redwood.example.com in us-west-2 and eu-central-1 starting ~10:12 UTC. Oncall: Elena.
Elena (oncall): Ack. Spreading to #incidents. @Tom @Priya @Marco please stand by.
Tom (sre): Joining. Which frontends affected? Any error samples?
Elena (oncall): Error rate dashboard: TLS handshake fail rate went from 1% -> 48% within 7m. Customers reporting 502 and aborts.
Marco (eng): I see deploy-bot ran "cert-rotate" pipeline at 10:08 UTC for edge-proxies. It rotated to a new intermediate chain from vendor.
deploy-bot: deploy: cert-rotate started service=edge-proxy region=eu-central-1 run=rot-20260315-09 at 2026-03-15T10:08:11Z.
Priya (netops): I'll run path checks. We had a peering change last month in us-west-2 with an MTU override=1452 on transit attachment; might be related.
Tom (sre): Can someone paste an example curl and openssl output? Need to see where handshake stops.
Jay (cs): Customer logs: "TLS handshake timeout" and some "ERR_CONNECTION_RESET" from mobile SDKs.
Marco (eng): App process logs show: `BIO_read() return error` and `ssl->handshake_state stuck`.
Elena (oncall): Quick curl from a compute host in eu-central-1:

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health
*   Trying 10.20.9.77...
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.20.9.77) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* OpenSSL SSL_connect: Connection reset by peer in connection to api.redwood.example.com:443
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: Connection reset by peer in connection to api.redwood.example.com:443
```

Tom (sre): Okay server is resetting before ServerHello. Marco can you run `openssl s_client -connect` from same host with -debug?
Marco (eng): Ran from host:

```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -msg -debug
>>> TLS 1.3, ClientHello, length = 512
<<< (no response)
socket: Connection reset by peer
140...: error:10000077:SSL routines:OPENSSL_internal:SSL handshake failure:ssl/statem/handshake.c:??
```

Priya (netops): Running tracepath shows PMTU drop at transit-node-b in us-west-2 with reported pmtu 1452:

```
$ tracepath 10.20.9.77
 1?: [LOCALHOST] pmtu 1500
 1:  10.0.2.1                                           0.220ms pmtu 1500
 2:  transit-node-b                                     2.310ms pmtu 1452
 3:  10.20.9.77                                         2.412ms
```

Priya (netops): tcpdump on edge-proxy shows many retransmits and ICMP "fragmentation needed" from transit-node-b with mtu=1452. Packets with DF set are being dropped.

```
12:10:14.543210 IP 10.0.8.12.443 > 10.0.2.45.51234: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, ack 1, win 256, length 1460
12:10:14.543227 IP 10.0.8.12 > 10.0.2.45: ICMP destination unreachable (frag needed and DF set), mtu 1452
12:10:14.543260 IP 10.0.8.12.443 > 10.0.2.45.51234: Flags [P.], seq 1461:2921, ack 1, length 1460 (retransmission)
```

Tom (sre): Large TLS ServerHello+Certificate (and OCSP stapled responses) can create bigger packets. If DF is set and PMTU discovery fails (ICMP blocked), large outgoing packets are dropped leading to handshake deadlock. Hypothesis: cert rotation introduced bigger chain or OCSP stapling length changed -> exceed PMTU -> dropped -> handshake resets.
Elena (oncall): Let's log hypotheses: A) Rotation produced larger cert chain / stapled response (Marco) B) Peering MTU lowered to 1452 and ICMP blocked (Priya) C) LB changed to set DF or disable MSS clamping (infra) D) DNS or routing unrelated.
Priya (netops): Confirming: firewall rules between transit-node-b and edge-proxies are dropping ICMP type 3 code 4. Also found the peering MTU override was set last month with no MSS-clamp.
Marco (eng): Checking rotated cert file: new chain + stapled OCSP = 4.8KB payload (old ~2.7KB). That increases TLS flight >1 packet. I uploaded the cert chain to s3://incidents/1876549999/cert-chain.pem and the rotation pipeline logs s3://incidents/1876549999/rotate-log.txt
Tom (sre): Immediate mitigations options: 1) rollback cert rotation 2) enable MSS clamping on transit-node-b and allow ICMP frag-needed 3) enable tcp_mtu_probing on LB nodes 4) split cert chain via using shorter chain if vendor offers. Which order?
Elena (oncall): Low-risk first: netops apply MSS clamp and allow ICMP. Marco trigger rollback if rollout continues.
Priya (netops): MSS clamp applied (set-mss 1400) on transit-node-b at 10:18 UTC. Also added temporary firewall allow for ICMP type 3 code 4.
Marco (eng): Rotation job was in-progress across some AZs; triggered rollback at 10:19:01. deploy-bot: rollback started rot-20260315-09 at 2026-03-15T10:19:01Z.
deploy-bot: rollback completed at 2026-03-15T10:21:10Z.
Marco (eng): Rollback done. Edge-proxy TLS flights now smaller (confirmed by pcap).
Tom (sre): Observability: handshake error rate fell from 48% -> 2% by 10:23 UTC. Customer errors decreased.
Jay (cs): Notified affected customers; one large customer reported interruption stopped ~10:23 UTC.
Elena (oncall): Collecting artifacts and building timeline.
Elena (oncall): Timeline (UTC):
- 10:08:11 deploy-bot: cert-rotate job started (partial rollout)
- 10:11:30 first error spike alerted by monitoring -> incident-bot pager
- 10:12-10:18 handshake failures escalate across regions
- 10:18:05 netops applied MSS clamp + allow ICMP
- 10:19:01 rollback triggered
- 10:21:10 rollback complete
- 10:23:00 metrics normalized

Tom (sre): Artifact checklist for RCA: rotation pipeline logs, rotated cert pkcs7/chain, pcap/tcpdump from edge-proxy, transit-node-b router config and ACL diffs, firewall logs showing ICMP denies, tracepath outputs, customer error logs. Please upload to s3://incidents/1876549999/.
Marco (eng): Uploaded rotate-log.txt and cert-chain.pem to s3://incidents/1876549999/. Pcap from edge node uploaded as edge-pcap.pcap.gz.
Priya (netops): Router config diffs and firewall deny logs uploaded.
Elena (oncall): Hypothesis tracking: 
- Hypothesis A (Confirmed): Rotated cert + stapled OCSP increased TLS flight size causing PMTU exceed on path with MTU 1452 while ICMP frag-needed was blocked. Evidence: cert payload size, tracepath PMTU=1452, tcpdump shows frag-needed ICMP and drops, service recovered after MSS clamp+rollback. Status: Confirmed.
- Hypothesis B (Investigate): LB kernel/sysctl disabled mtuprobing and there is no MSS clamping by default. Evidence: LB sysctl `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` = 0 on some nodes. Action: Marco to enable mtuprobing and add a preflight check in rotation pipeline.
- Hypothesis C (Less likely): Vendor served an unexpectedly large stapled OCSP for specific cert chain. Evidence: need vendor cert response. Action: Marco to ask CA.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Marco (eng): Postmortem write-up for cert rotation pipeline and add size gate (prevent rotations if chain+OCSP > 3.5KB). Upload draft by 2026-03-18.
- Priya (netops): Apply org-wide MSS-clamp on peerings where MTU < 1500 and audit ICMP policies; propose permanent firewall change to allow frag-needed for PMTU, due 2026-03-20.
- Tom (sre): Add monitoring alert for sudden TLS "no ServerHello" pattern and for cert chain size changes at rotation time; update runbook. Due 2026-03-17.
- Jay (cs): Send customer post-incident summary and update SLAs as needed.

Priya (netops): Recommended policy change: require MSS-clamp when setting non-standard MTU on transit attachments.
Marco (eng): For durable mitigation: enable `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on LB fleet, add cert size check to rotation pipeline, and work with CA to request smaller stapled OCSP responses if possible.
Tom (sre): I'll create a follow-up ticket to update the oncall runbook with PMTU troubleshooting steps and include tcpdump sample checks.
Elena (oncall): Great job everyone. I'll convert this thread to the incident postmortem skeleton and tag owners. Moving detailed discussion to #postmortems. Closing incident now.
incident-bot: Incident resolved. Duration ~11m. Severity: S2.
Jay (cs): Customer communication sent 11:05 UTC.
Elena (oncall): Final note: artifacts retained at s3://incidents/1876549999/. Postmortem owner Marco.
